title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
read_level: full main text (Secs 1-9) plus appendix A protocol and lineage table; appendices C-H skimmed
why_wsp: Three frontier LLMs ('writers') write every weight of target models without gradients, either into fixed released architectures/given Transformers or into architectures they design themselves (sparse fact tables), from ten labeled examples in a sandbox.
domain: multiple-choice science QA (ARC), plus SciQ, OpenBookQA, MMLU, SQuAD, CNN/DailyMail, CIFAR-10, AG News
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (high reasoning effort), GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra; Claude Fable 5.2 where stated
target: released architectures (15) of 129M-2.6B from random init; given two-layer Transformer (0.03M-3.96M); LLM-designed sparse-table models 0.11M-3.35M; authors' associative-memory-based model 0.09M-6.24M; pretrained checkpoints in Sec 7.1
interface: code/tensor tools (writer delivers word list, plain-text fact files and build.py compiled to tensors on CPU; edit scripts for released checkpoints)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (writer self-generated practice questions inside a run; lineages pass parent model and one validation accuracy per generation, better of two runs, up to 10 generations)
self_editing: no; writers build separate target models
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Released architectures from random init: "the median run changes 80% of the parameters (range 35% to 100%)" (App A). Pretrained: "In most runs (48 of 87 across the three LLMs), the LLM changes under 1% of the weights." (Sec 7.1)

headline_results.claim: LLM-designed table beats released Transformer with ~1,800x fewer params
headline_results.quote: an LLM-designed model achieves higher ARC test accuracy than the most accurate released Transformer that the same LLM wrote while using about 1,800x fewer parameters

headline_results.claim: Pretrained fine-tuned models far more accurate
headline_results.quote: pretrained models fine-tuned on ARC remain far more accurate, with Qwen3.5-0.8B at 82.1%
a removed line changes 0.5 to 1.8 answers on average (Table 5)

headline_results.claim: Written Transformers below BM25 over own text
headline_results.quote: The six written two-layer Transformers of Claude Opus 5.5 all score below BM25 over their own text, by 8.0 points on average.
a same-sized Transformer is 7 times slower at the first-generation size and 17 times slower at the fifth-generation size

headline_results.claim: Most LLM-designed models slower on GPU
headline_results.quote: Across 46 LLM-designed variants (Figure 4a), only one beats a same-sized Transformer at its fastest input, and the median is 9.4x slower.

headline_results.claim: Pretrained WSP mostly small edits, accuracy unchanged
headline_results.quote: accuracy stays within one point of the checkpoint's in 43 of these 48 runs
networks written by Claude Opus 5.5 reach only 21% to 28% across eight fixed architectures, against 10% chance

cost.claim: LLM cost per run/lineage in Table 3
cost.where: Table 3 (Claude Opus 5.5; generation 5 lineage $144; GPT-6 Astra associative-memory generation 8 $490)

cost.quote: answering the 3,530 test questions on one RTX 3090 in 18 ms

baselines_and_controls: Gradient descent from random init on same architectures and on LLM-designed-size Transformer/MLP with 3,358 labels; pretrained fine-tuned models (gemma-3-270m-it, UltraBERT-150M, Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3.5-0.8B); BM25 over the writer's own text; forbidding practice questions; forbidding fact rows; single-best-fact ablation; line-removal locality test; test-set overlap analysis; cross-benchmark transfer.
runs_and_variance: Two runs per generation (better passes on); several tables average two runs (Tables 4, 8); line-removal test on 40 random lines per model; no confidence intervals reported in main text.
robustness_of_edits: Transfer to other benchmarks tested (SciQ ~50%, OpenBookQA 30-36%, MMLU near chance); warm-starting gradient descent from a written network tested on AG News; no quantization/fine-tuning survival test of edits.
verification: none (sandbox checks for disallowed data/network; shape checks; static syntax check forbidding Python conditionals in free design)
memorization_vs_reasoning: Overlap of written text with ARC test set is about as often as with unseen comparable questions; deleting overlapping lines barely changes accuracy (Sec 5.2, App D). Paper states it cannot separate a structure chosen because it suits writing from one chosen because retrieval is familiar (Sec 5.2).
limitations_stated: Written models only recall stated facts, no multi-step chaining or learned representations; ARC-Challenge stays near 38%; MMLU at chance; claim limited to writing from random init without running on data; speed advantage bounded by concept count; single GPU type measured.
code_or_data: none found (PDF header shows 'Code' and 'Project page' labels but no URL recoverable from the PDF text or link annotations)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming blog
Dugan et al. 2025 hand-constructed fact-storing MLPs
notes_for_survey: When allowed to choose architecture, all three writer LLMs built sparse fact tables read by a fixed procedure rather than Transformers; written Transformers scored below BM25 over the same written text. Authors propose a hashed associative-memory forward pass for fast inference; pretrained fine-tuned models remain far more accurate on ARC.
